dedupe_keys.name: fabric nsf funded research infrastructure to prototype networking and computing beyond the current internet

description: FABRIC is a research infrastructure for prototyping and validating new network and computing ideas beyond the scope of the current internet, funded by a series of US National Science Foundation grants. Researchers reserve resources on it through the FABRIC portal and run experiments; the project runs training (the KNIT workshops and the Mastering FABRIC webinar series), a knowledge base and forums. Coverage: a research network whose sites and capacities were not read from the pages opened. Recent project news covers AI-driven networking and cybersecurity, in-network computing at high speed and distributed storage to preserve and reuse experiment data. Format and access: a web portal (version 1.10.4 at the time read) with accounts under an acceptable use policy; the knowledge base and portal pages are public. Licence: not applicable to the testbed; the terms of use were not read. Caveats: the portal is a script-driven application, so the site list, hardware and eligibility were not read; access is aimed at the research community. Simulation uses: experiments on programmable wide-area networks to test routing, security and resilience ideas at scale. Related records: the PAWR wireless testbeds (platform-nsf-pawr-advanced-wireless-testbeds) are a companion NSF programme, and CORE (platform-core) is a laptop-scale network emulator.
